Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.prefs

Class DesktopConfig

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.prefs.DesktopConfig
public final class DesktopConfig extends Object
User-facing desktop configuration: taskbar thickness, position, icon size, the Swing application UI font, and the taskbar auto-hide toggle.

The settings live in lg3d-core so both the scene-manager taskbar and the (demo-apps) Control Center can share one model - demo-apps depends on core, never the reverse. Values are persisted through LgPreferencesHelper (i.e. java.util.prefs); setters only mutate in-memory state, so a caller batches changes and then invokes save().

The instance is a lazily-created singleton (get()) that reads the stored preferences once on first access. After a save(), editors post a DesktopConfigChangeEvent so live consumers (the taskbar, the Swing look-and-feel) re-read the model and re-apply.

    • isFrostedGlass

      public boolean isFrostedGlass()
      Whether decorated Frame3D windows use the GPU frosted-glass body (FrostedGlassPanel) instead of the fixed-function 2006 GlassyPanel. Decorations and the taskbar shelf listen for DesktopConfigChangeEvent and flip their glass Switch in place, so a change takes effect immediately on every open window and the bar - no restart needed.

    • setFrostedGlass

      public void setFrostedGlass(boolean frostedGlass)

    • isRoundedCorners

      public boolean isRoundedCorners()
      Whether the GPU frosted glass of window decorations renders with anti-aliased rounded corners (true) or square corners (false). The frosted taskbar shelf is deliberately excluded - it always keeps square corners - and the fixed-function GlassyPanel is always square. On DesktopConfigChangeEvent every open decoration rewrites the frosted corner radius live, so a change takes effect immediately on existing windows.

    • setRoundedCorners

      public void setRoundedCorners(boolean roundedCorners)

    • getWindowOpacity

      public int getWindowOpacity()
      Opacity of the 2D desktop's application windows, as a percent of solid (100 = fully opaque). A window is a container of third-party Swing content that paints itself opaque, so the whole window - title bar, border and the application's own panel - fades together; fading only the chrome would show nothing through an opaque panel. Read at paint time by DesktopTransparency, which repaints every open window on DesktopConfigChangeEvent and on Desktop2D.applyDesktopConfig(), so a change lands without a restart.

    • setWindowOpacity

      public void setWindowOpacity(int percent)

    • getTaskbarOpacity

      public int getTaskbarOpacity()
      Opacity of the 2D desktop's taskbar, as a percent of solid. Only the bar's own backdrop fades - its buttons, labels and tray indicators stay fully opaque, because a bar you cannot read is not a bar.

    • setTaskbarOpacity

      public void setTaskbarOpacity(int percent)

    • getWidgetOpacity

      public int getWidgetOpacity()
      Opacity of the desktop widgets (the cards the widget layer drops on the wallpaper), as a percent of solid. The whole card fades, so its text keeps its contrast against its own background. Applies to the 2D desktop only: the same cards hosted through a SwingNode on the 3D desktop stay solid, because their opaque background is what makes that capture path reliable.

    • setWidgetOpacity

      public int getNotificationOpacity()
      Opacity of the transient notification cards (toasts), as a percent of solid. Only the card's fill fades; the title and message paint fully opaque, so a notification that is meant to be readable stays readable.

    • clampOpacity

      public static int clampOpacity(int percent)
      Keeps a surface opacity between MIN_SURFACE_OPACITY and MAX_SURFACE_OPACITY; an out-of-range or nonsensical stored value (a hand-edited preference) degrades to the nearer bound rather than to an invisible or unpainted surface. Public because DesktopTransparency clamps the same way when a caller sets a value programmatically.

    • getCustomShortcuts

      public String getCustomShortcuts()
      The encoded custom keyboard-shortcut overrides: a ;-separated list of action=keyspec pairs (e.g. run-dialog=alt F2) that replace the matching default bindings. Never null; empty means "all defaults". Read by Desktop2D when it builds the shortcut table.

    • setCustomShortcuts

      public void setCustomShortcuts(String encoded)

    • parseCustomShortcuts

      public static Map<String,String> parseCustomShortcuts(String encoded)
      Parses the encoded custom-shortcut string into an action -> keystroke-spec map, skipping blank/malformed entries (a keystroke spec may contain spaces but never ; or =, so the split is unambiguous). Pure so it can be unit-tested headless.

    • serializeCustomShortcuts

      public static String serializeCustomShortcuts(Map<String,String> actionToSpec)
      Serializes an action -> keystroke-spec map back into the encoded action=keyspec;... form, skipping null/blank keys or values. The inverse of parseCustomShortcuts(String).
